title: 2000 AMC 8 Problem 9
statement: Three-digit powers of \(2\) and \(5\) are used in this “cross-number” puzzle. What is the only possible digit for the outlined square? \[\begin{array}{lcl} \textbf{\text{ACROSS}} & & \textbf{\text{DOWN}} \\ \textbf{2. } 2^m & & \textbf{1. } 5^n \end{array}\]

solutions.text:
The only \(3\)-digit powers of \(5\) are \(125\) and \(625.\) This means that the \(2\) spot is filled with a \(2.\)

The only \(3\)-digit power of \(2\) beginning with a \(2\) is \(256,\) so the outlined square is filled with a \(6.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: The across entry is a three-digit power of \(2\) starting with \(2\)
